brief: UBS's Top 10 Q&A ties Fed Chair Warsh's hawkish shift, reinforced by 162,000 August payrolls versus a 55,000 consensus, to a raised 2026 hike forecast (two 25bp moves, fed funds to 4.00-4.25%) and higher Treasury yield forecasts (2-year to 4.25%, 10-year to 4.5%). UBS argues the same growth strength behind that pivot supports a constructive equity outlook, so it stays constructive on equities while pushing diversification: AI capex, power and resources, and Longevity remain core theses, but concentration risk, 40% of self-managed investors hold over half their book in 10 stocks or fewer, argues for broadening into cyclicals, Europe, and Asia, where earnings growth is forecast to outpace the US. Gold faces near-term pressure from higher real rates and a stronger dollar but keeps its strategic hedge role given persistent central-bank buying. The US-Iran conflict has disrupted Strait of Hormuz shipping and lifted European gas and Brent prices, but adaptation has limited the economic shock, so UBS favors diversified commodity exposure rather than a directional call. Higher-for-longer yields narrow the case for bonds over cash, pushing UBS toward diversified income and disciplined cash planning.

cards.claim: UBS now expects the Federal Reserve to raise rates twice in 2026, in 25-basis-point moves in September and December, taking the federal funds target range to 4.00-4.25%.
cards.anchor: We now expect 25-basis-point rate hikes in September and December, taking the federal funds target range to 4.00-4.25%.
